sections.html:
Utah County's Orem sits roughly 45 miles south of Salt Lake City, near the eastern edge of Utah Lake. Its 18.57 square miles of land lie at about 4,767 feet, bordered by Provo on the east and south, Vineyard on the west and Lindon on the north.

Two roads organize the map. Interstate 15 runs down the west side with four interchanges inside the city, and US 89 (State Street) cuts through the middle on a northwest to southeast line. Cross streets such as 800 North (Canyon Parkway), 1600 North, University Parkway and Geneva Road carry state route numbers. Buyers ask how far a house is from State Street, University Parkway and the freeway.

sections.h2: Where the name and the grid came from
sections.html: Settled in 1877, Orem was first called Sharon and then Provo Bench. The name Orem arrived in 1914 for Walter C. Orem, president of the Salt Lake and Utah Railroad, and the town was chartered on May 5, 1919. Early farmers built along the territorial highway, now State Street, and that pattern still shows. Older lots near State Street and the original grid look quite different from newer tracts built later.

Orem counted 98,129 people in 2020 and is estimated at 95,214 for July 1, 2025, which makes it the fifth most populous city in Utah. Owners hold a little more than half of households.

These are citywide medians, not a value for any single house. Condition, lot and street all pull a real sale away from the middle. If your house is near a campus or a station, mention it, but expect a buyer to compare it against the whole range of Orem prices before settling on a number.

sections.h2: What kinds of homes does Orem have?
sections.html:
Detached houses, townhomes and apartments all appear in the mix. Of 29,593 occupied units in the 2021 American Community Survey, 17,913 (60.5%) were owner-occupied and 11,680 (39.5%) were rented.

  • Single-family homes: 16,509 units, or 55.8% of occupied housing
  • Twinhomes and townhomes: 3,227 units, or 10.9%
  • Buildings with 10 or more apartments or condos: 4,434 units, or 15.0%
  • Mobile homes and other types: 575 units, or 1.9%

A house that has been a rental for years can need different handling from an owner-occupied one, since leases, tenants and put-off repairs all shape how a sale goes.

An accessory apartment is allowed inside a main home as long as the owner lives in the house or in the apartment. The city counted 752 legal ones as of June 2023, with 30 added in 2022 and 23 more in the first half of 2023.

A basement apartment that was never registered, or one a past owner rented out while living elsewhere, will draw questions from a buyer's inspector. Detached units are a newer topic. Orem has never allowed them, and the city's proposed response to state law S.B. 284 would keep them out of front yards and bar short-term rental use. The statute applies to lots of 11,000 square feet or more. Call the planning office for the current rule if a detached unit is part of your plan or your buyer's.

A FrontRunner commuter rail station sits on the west side of I-15, tied to the Utah Valley University campus by a pedestrian bridge. UVX, a bus rapid transit line shared with Provo, runs from Orem Central Station through UVU and University Parkway toward Provo. Workers average a 20.1 minute commute. Homes within walking range of the station or a UVX stop can feature that in a listing.

UVU enrolls more than 43,000 undergraduates, so rental demand near campus is a real part of the housing story.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Orem, and what changes in 2027?
sections.html:
Right now Alpine School District handles Orem schools, but it ends on July 1, 2027. A June 2026 resource agreement places Orem in the new Timpanogos district, joined by Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard. Voters backed the split in the 2024 general election, board members were chosen in 2025 and superintendents were hired in 2026.

Parents ask which district a house belongs to, and for Orem listings that answer shifts during the sale year. Look up the exact address on the boundary map.

Utah County sends Orem's tax bills. Around the end of July comes a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Changes, and any market-value appeal must reach the Board of Equalization by September 15. The tax notice itself lands between mid and late October.

Primary homes get a 45% residential exemption, which leaves tax on 55% of market value. The home must be lived in for at least 183 consecutive days a year by the owner, a relative or a full-time tenant. A rental with no eligible full-time occupant counts as secondary and is taxed on full value. New owners may receive a declaration form after the deed changes hands.

The Utah County Treasurer, at 801-851-8255, answers payoff questions. The Recorder at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo files deeds, though its staff will not draft documents, advise on law or search titles.

The Wasatch Fault stretches about 240 miles in ten segments, five active, and Orem lies near the active Provo segment. That one last produced a large event roughly 200 to 700 years ago. About 80% of Utah residents live along the fault. Inspectors may mention chimney bracing, water heater straps and foundation ties, and older brick houses attract the most comments. Selling as-is keeps all of that off your repair list.

sections.h2: Selling an Orem house for cash
sections.html:
People call about inherited houses, worn-out rentals, basement apartments with no paperwork and moves on a short fuse. Tell us about the property, we look at it, and we price it by condition.

Everything is bought as-is, so skip the paint, patching and cleaning. Closing runs through a title or escrow company, which also submits the deed to the Utah County Recorder, so ask that agent for timing. With a tenant in place, share the lease terms and any move-out date during your first call and we will build them into the offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Orem house if it has an unregistered basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. Because the owner has to live in the house or the apartment, an inspector for a conventional buyer may want proof the unit is legal. We take the house as it is, with no need to settle that first.

faqs.q: How long does Utah County take to record a deed for an Orem sale?
faqs.a: Your title or escrow company submits the deed to the Utah County Recorder, which records documents that meet state rules. Your closing agent can give you the expected turnaround.

faqs.q: Does a tenant in my Orem house stop me from selling?
faqs.a: No, a tenant does not block a sale. Share the lease and the move-out date with us up front so the offer can account for them.

faqs.q: Which school district will Orem homes belong to after 2027?
faqs.a: The new Timpanogos district takes over Orem when Alpine School District is dissolved on July 1, 2027. The boundary map will confirm your street.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an Orem property valuation?
faqs.a: File by September 15, for any reason. After that, a late appeal runs through March 31 but only if it meets extra criteria and the Board of Equalization accepts it.
